dok_rationale: Part (c) weighs competing descriptions using two graph features and explains why a typical value alone cannot represent the full distribution.
stem: The histogram shows how long it took 40 students to get to school one morning, in minutes. Two students described the distribution.\par\smallskip \textbf{Ana:} ``Roughly symmetric, centered near 20 minutes, spread from 5 to 45 minutes.''\par \textbf{Ben:} ``Skewed right with a peak in the 10--20 minute interval; most students take under 30 minutes; one student at about 70 minutes is an outlier.''
first_take: Whose description do you trust more, Ana's or Ben's? One sentence. No wrong answers yet.

parts.label: a
parts.prompt: Which interval has the tallest bar?

parts.label: b
parts.prompt: In two or three sentences, describe the commute times: shape, a typical value, overall spread, and one unusual feature. Use minutes.

parts.label: c
parts.prompt: Whose description is better supported? Use two graph features to defend your choice. Explain why reporting only a typical commute time would leave a reader with an incomplete picture.

answers.b: One peak and a longer right tail. A typical commute is around 20--30 minutes; values extend from the 0--10 bin to the 70--80 bin. There are no times in 60--70 and one time in 70--80 minutes. Exact minimum, maximum, and mean cannot be read from these bins.
answers.c: Ben's description is better supported by the longer right tail and the isolated observation in 70--80 minutes after an empty interval. His `about 70' is only a rough location; the exact time is unknown. A typical time around 20--30 minutes leaves out the students with much longer commutes, so the spread and unusual value belong in the report too. Accept other pairs of distinct relevant features, including the spread beyond 45 that contradicts Ana.

expectedElements.description: Chooses Ben and links one graph feature to the disagreement (tail, actual spread, peak, or fraction under 30)
Uses a second distinct, relevant feature to support Ben or contradict Ana; e.g. isolated high bin, gap, or spread beyond 45
Explains that a typical time alone hides the long commutes or overall spread

scoringGuide.E: All three elements are correct and linked to this problem. Accept equivalent plain-language reasoning.
scoringGuide.P: At least one element includes a correct evidence-to-reason link, but another is missing or incorrect.
scoringGuide.I: No correct evidence-to-reason link; only a choice, copied numbers, or unsupported statements.

commonMistakes: Treating the isolated long commute as typical
Naming right skew without locating the tail
Reading exact endpoints or a mean from grouped data

dok_rationale: Constructing a display to match a multi-feature verbal description requires coordinating shape, modality, and an outlier in one sketch, but follows one known procedure.
stem: Sketch a dotplot of 15 quiz scores (0--10) that is skewed LEFT, unimodal, and has one low outlier. Then write the one sentence a reader would need in order to describe it in context.

answers.a: Any dotplot with a cluster near 8--10, a thin tail to the left, and an isolated dot near 1--2. Sentence names the variable (quiz score), the shape, the center region, and the outlier.
